title: Tony Canadeo and the Packers at the club
summary: A story of meeting football player Tony Canadeo, a Gonzaga classmate, at a Los Angeles club, and Rowles's contempt for him.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: And I remember Tony Canadeo(?) was there when I was there. Years and years later, I was in Los Angeles, and I was playing with my trio, and the team that he was playing was... What was it? The one that won for so many years. Canadeo and the big-time coach that was such a wheel... Bart Starr...you know who I'm talking about. Detroit? No, it
I have no idea. [VINCE LOMBARDI/GREEN BAY PACKERS]

Anyway, he was a backfield coach. So the owner of the club said... They were out... They had decided to celebrate at that club that night; they had won the Super Bowl. And they all came out there, see, and he was there. And I told the boss, you know; I said, "I went to school with that guy, Canadeo." I didn't know him, but I went to school with him. Boy, he was snotty. This guy called him over, you know, and he said, "I'd like you to meet the guy that has the trio here; he says he went to Gonzaga, too." And Canadeo says, "Oh yeah? When were you there?" And I said, "I was there when you were there. And your hair was gray then!" And he says, "Well, I didn't know you." I said, "Well, I didn't know you either." And he says, "Do you play Dixieland?" I said, "No. I play just exactly what I want, and I don't play Dixieland" -- and I turned away and walked away from him. He was a real bad guy, as far as I was concerned. I ignored him. And they carried on with their whoop-de-do, you know...
What was the name of that team?
Yeah, well, you didn't miss anything. I have more fun watching tennis. That's my game.
